newsitem.title: USA: Stocks hold their ground ahead of Fed rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Stocks hold their ground ahead of Fed rate decision.

text.p: Stocks held modest gains Tuesday as the market geared up for a widely anticipated hike in short-term interest rates by the Federal Reserve.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 8.69 points at 6,913.94.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a 13-9 margin on active New York Stock Exchange volume of 251 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index was up 6.65 points at 1,249.29.
Analysts said a quarter-point increase already was priced into the market, and they believed that Monday's 100-point leap in the Dow index was the equivelent of a relief rally.
"We are getting a relief rally before the Fed tightening," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyons & Ross.
"There might not be any reaction if the Fed tightens by 25 basis points as we have already had one. But if it does not tighten, the market may be very disappointed for a few hours," Blumberg said.

The central bank's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee started its meeting at 9 a.m. EST (1400 GMT) Tuesday and following recent practice, the decision should be known around 2:15 p.m. (1915 GMT).

Recent comments by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan appear to have conditioned financial markets to expect a token rise in interest rates as the central bank aims to sustain moderate economic growth and head off potential inflationary pressures that could emerge by late this year or early next year.
A larger rate increase, however, might trigger a sell-off while a decision not to tighten could prompt a rally, analysts said.

In the bond market, the key 30-year Treasury bond was up a quarter point, sending its yield down to 6.90 percent from Monday's close of 6.92 percent. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Defensive issues, which are stocks that do well regardless of the pace of the economy, were also stronger. Philip Morris Cos. was up 2 at 117-7/8 and Merck & Co. gained 1-1/4 at 91-1/8.
"Essentially, the defensive side of the market has reasserted itself," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.
"The message of the stock market today is that the Fed will not only raise rates, but its strategy will work in the sense that we will see the economy slow. In time, though, not right away," he said.
Among special situations, Cintas Corp. rose 2 to 54 after Barrington Research raised its rating on the stock, and Integrated Systems Inc. fell 5-3/4 to 11-3/8 on a downgrading by Hambrecht & Quist.
